    16  # Principal ideal rings, principal ideal domains, and Bézout rings
    17  
    18  A principal ideal ring (PIR) is a ring in which all left ideals are principal. A
    19  principal ideal domain (PID) is an integral domain which is a principal ideal ring.
    20  
    21  The definition of `IsPrincipalIdealRing` can be found in `Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Span.lean`.
    22  
    23  ## Main definitions
    24  
    25  Note that for principal ideal domains, one should use
    26  `[IsDomain R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R]`. There is no explicit definition of a PID.
    27  Theorems about PID's are in the `PrincipalIdealRing` namespace.
    28  
    29  - `IsBezout`: the predicate saying that every finitely generated left ideal is principal.
    30  - `generator`: a generator of a principal ideal (or more generally submodule)
    31  - `to_uniqueFactorizationMonoid`: a PID is a unique factorization domain
    32  
    33  ## Main results
    34  
    35  - `Ideal.IsPrime.to_maximal_ideal`: a non-zero prime ideal in a PID is maximal.
    36  - `EuclideanDomain.to_principal_ideal_domain` : a Euclidean domain is a PID.
    37  - `IsBezout.nonemptyGCDMonoid`: Every Bézout domain is a GCD domain.
